EF21 theory supplies a nonempty stable interval near zero, while the map is unstable for large s, leaving the unique positive root as the exact frontier. The n→∞ two-state limit has Jury interval 0<s<6.

value.rationale: The worker-count law is a natural exact benchmark for a central distributed error-feedback architecture. It quantifies a concrete averaging mechanism behind large admissible steps, separates mean-square stability from generic sufficient bounds, and supplies an exact regression test across n.

final_claim: For distributed EF21 on identical scalar quadratics with independent half-dropout compressors, mean-square stability for every square-integrable exchangeable initialization holds exactly for 0<s<6n/(n+8); the frontier increases from 2/3 at one worker to the deterministic lagged-gradient ceiling 6 as n→∞.
limitations: Identical scalar curvatures, independent Bernoulli(1/2) compressor events and exchangeable square-integrable initialization only.
No almost-sure Lyapunov or heterogeneous-client claim.
